name: Susan Electricals India Ltd
title: Susan Electricals India Ltd - 544793 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Susan Electricals is shifting mix toward HT/MV covered conductors (HT ~30% of Q2 sales vs 0.75% in H1 FY26) while H1 EBITDA margin slipped to ~11.8%, with receivables and capacity expansion still pending.

triggers.label: New land for 20,000 capacity expansion
triggers.quote: we are acquiring a parcel of land

guidance.quote: maintained in the range of 11.5% to 12%

summary.headline: Susan Electricals H1 FY27 revenue rose 190% to ₹202 crore and PAT rose 191% to ₹13.15 crore, while H1 EBITDA margin fell to 11.77% from 13.13%.
summary.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 revenue of ₹202 crore (up 190% YoY from ₹69 crore) and PAT of ₹13.15 crore (up 191% from ₹4.53 crore), with EBITDA up 160% to ₹23.78 crore. The company is shifting its mix toward HT and CCV-based products, with HT share of the Q2 mix reaching about 30% from 0.75% in H1 FY26. Order book stood at ₹147 crore plus ₹200 crore of L1/L2/L3/L4 pipeline. Margins were lower YoY, which management attributed to one-time metal-price gains in H1 FY26 and an expected sustainable 11.5%–12% range. Management flagged a land acquisition and a new plant, with a CCV line commissioning as the key near-term milestone.

segments.name: HT (high tension) cables/conductors
segments.commentary: Share of revenue rose from 0.75% in H1 FY26 to about 30% in Q2 FY27; HT is 54 crore of the 147 crore order book. Q2 EBITDA margin was 13.13%, and management guided HT EBITDA margin at 12%–14%.

segments.name: MV (medium voltage) products
segments.commentary: Management cited 69 crore of order book, the largest component (almost half), and an EBITDA margin of 10%–13%. Q2 EBITDA margin was 11.82%.

segments.name: LT (low tension) cables
segments.commentary: LT share fell from 46% in H1 FY26 to about 31% in Q2 FY27; LT order book is 24 crore; LT EBITDA margin of 9%–11.5%, Q2 at 11%. Company is deliberately reducing LT exposure given competition.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 to be stronger than H1, citing seasonality (government and EPC targets, with February and March typically stronger) and a healthy pipeline.
Blended EBITDA margin expected in the 11.5%–12% range going forward; management called Q2's 18.18% not sustainable.
Target product mix of 33%-33%-33% across HT, MV and LT, with HT and MV reaching 40%–45% each and LT at 10%–20% over time.
Installed capacity targeted to rise from 7,500 tons to 20,000 tons after the new plant, with the new location expected to be operational around end-FY28 and construction underway.
Management is not giving a specific revenue number for the 347 crore visibility; it said about 90% is scheduled to be executed by March 31, 2027.
capex_capacity: CCV (continuous curing vulcanisation) line has arrived at the factory and is in installation; commissioning is expected in the next few months. CCV is mandatory for HT projects in most states.
Winding-wire capacity is planned to rise from 4,200 tons to 5,500 tons; total manufacturing capacity is targeted at 7,500 tons, with the new plant to take it to 20,000 tons.

A land parcel is being acquired (price about ₹10,000 per sq yard versus ~₹1 lakh per sq yard for UPSIDC area), with plans to shift 1–2 factories there; the funding mix is internal accruals and bank loans.

Current borrowings are backed by ₹48 crore of FDs (including ₹5.62 crore pledged mutual funds) as collateral for cash-credit limits; management expects these to be released once the new land is acquired.
Management said the new facility can be built within 1.5–2 years, with a shift in FY27-28 and FY28-29 ramp-up; sheds are used to speed construction.
Management said CTC (continuously transposed conductor) R&D is underway, with no supply to date; the company will announce when it starts.
demand_pricing: Order book: ₹147 crore as of September 30, 2026, of which HT is ₹54 crore and MV is ₹69 crore, and LT is ₹24 crore. An additional ₹200 crore of L1–L4 bids in progress gives combined visibility of ₹347 crore.
Q2 FY27 executed ₹107 crore against ₹111 crore of new orders won.
Management says it bids for HT tenders now that the CCV line is arriving, and it accepts many L2–L4 bids at its discretion.
Competition in LT has intensified, so management is cutting LT bids; it sees more attractive economics in HT and MV.
Private customers often buy at a base rate with metal-price variation included, while EPC customers are about 90% variation-inclusive. Government payments are 90–95% of receivables.
Customers include transformer manufacturers such as CG, CMI and Hitachi Energy (non-contractual). The company also supplies railways (RVNL, Coalfields).

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from 13.7% to 11.5%, and is 11.5%–12% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 FY26 included one-time metal-price gains. Adjusting for them, H1 FY27 margin is 11.77% against 13.13% in H1 FY26. FY26 full-year margin was 11.91%, and management expects 11.5%–12% with HT and MV mix gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected HT and MV contribution in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: HT was 30% of Q2 volume, MV 33%, and LT 31%. Management targets HT and MV at 40%–45% each and LT at 10%–20%.

qa_highlights.question: How will the land acquisition and expansion be funded, and will it stress working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Funding combines internal accruals, bank cash-credit and loans; collateral is ₹48 crore of FDs. Management said there is no stress and the company is cash-flow positive.

qa_highlights.question: Is cash flow positive, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash flow turned positive. Of ₹95 crore receivables, ₹25 crore is from September and not yet due, ₹44 crore was collected in October, and about 5% exceeds 180 days.

qa_highlights.question: Is H2 seasonally stronger?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said EPC and government targets push activity into October–March, with H2 typically 25%–40% stronger, particularly in February and March.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pursue exports or new product lines (capacitors, insulators)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no export plans for now; it is focused on HT, MV and LT cables and holds 12 BIS certifications.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the HT certification to 33 kV, CTC and defence?
qa_highlights.answer: HT is up to 33 kV, and the company plans to move to higher voltage levels once the BIS certification is obtained, which takes 2–3 months. CTC production is not yet supplied. The company is not yet a defence supplier.

risks_watch: Margin dilution: Q2 margin was 18.18% with metal-price gains, so H2 margin could be lower if metal prices fall or as LT mix changes.
Working capital: receivables at ₹95 crore and rising; collections and conversion to cash flow remain a management priority.
Execution: CCV line commissioning, HT tender wins and the new plant timeline (FY27-28/FY28-29) are key to the 20,000-ton target.
Funding and collateral: ₹48 crore of FDs backing CC limits; the land deal depends on bank release of collateral and a revaluation.
Disclosure: management corrected Q1 segment margin figures and declined to give specific forward numbers; monthly or quarterly realisation disclosure was requested but not committed.
Dependency on government and EPC payment cycles; MSME bill discounting via TReDS was classified in financing flows and may recur.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and mix shift, but cautious on margin sustainability and forward numbers; management repeatedly declined to give specific guidance on FY28 and revenue timing.
